standard_prerequisites.name: Degree of the dualizing sheaf in genus zero
Closed immersion from a degree-2 invertible sheaf
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns a basis of the three-dimensional space of global sections of L = omega_X^tensor -1 into a closed immersion into the projective plane.

standard_prerequisites.name: Plane-curve arithmetic genus
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemmas lemma-equation-plane-curve and lemma-genus-plane-curve
standard_prerequisites.use: Writes the equation F of the plane curve of degree d and forces d in {1, 2} from the vanishing genus.

core_obligations: Embedding (proof lines 2115-2124): L = omega_X^tensor -1 has degree 2, and a basis of its global sections gives a closed immersion into P^2, making X a plane curve of some degree d with equation F.

Degree pinning (proof lines 2125-2133): the genus-zero hypothesis restricts d to 1 or 2 by the plane-curve genus formula; F restricts to zero on the image so F(s_0, s_1, s_2) = 0 as a section of L^tensor 2; linear independence of the s_i excludes a linear F, so d = 2.
proof_roadmap: Identify the anti-dualizing sheaf as degree 2 and embed X into the plane.
Restrict the genus computation for plane curves to force d in {1, 2}.
Exclude d = 1 by the linear independence of the embedding sections.
difficulty_reason: The lemma classifies Gorenstein genus-zero proper curves as plane conics (statement lines 2108-2113). The proof (lines 2115-2133) is complete: the degree-two anti-dualizing sheaf, the closed immersion from its sections, the plane-curve genus restriction to degrees one and two, and the exclusion of the linear case by section independence. Every step is present with no omissions. H2: a short chain of correctly ordered standard inputs.
